content.text: Multiple threads accessed the same method at once, leading to faulty behavior.
Synchronization ensures that only one thread accesses a resource at a time.
Java achieves this using object monitors (locks). A thread acquires the monitor when entering a synchronized method/block, and releases it when exiting.
Using blocks is preferred when only part of the method needs synchronization.
